Accidental Release and Emergency Response Policies

Driscolls, Inc. is committed to providing a safe environment to its employees and surrounding communities.  This commitment is reflected in the safety and environmental programs that are implemented at the facility.  For example, written procedures have been created for operating the ammonia refrigeration system.  Only trained operators and the refrigeration contractor are permitted to perform system operations.  Driscolls, Inc. has also developed a robust maintenance program to ensure the equipment is in good operating condition.  All of these programs are geared towards the prevention of an accidental release at the facility.  In addition, these programs incorporate emergency procedures to mitigate the effects of a release if it does occur.  At such an event, emergency coordinators will assess the situation and notify outside responding agencies as necessary.

Stationary Source and Regulated Substance

Driscolls, Inc. is located at 1750 San Juan Road in Aromas, California.  The site is located near the community of Aromas, on the coast of central California, near the northern-most border of Monterey County, on 31.32 acres of property. The area immediately surrounding the facility is all agricultural land and is bordered on the north side by the Southern Pacific Railroad. In 1997 the facility expanded with the addition of a 60,000 sq. ft. pre-cooling and cold storage warehouse, along with a dedicated ammonia refrigeration system, (Main Cooler). Ammonia is used in the facilitys refrigeration system to provide cooling for the storage of berries, utilizing 12,800 lbs. 

The two condensers deliver high pressure liquid ammonia to the thermosyphon receiver, which in turn feeds the respective systems low pressure liquid ammonia recirculator. From the low pressure liquid ammonia recirculator, liquid ammonia is pumped to the individual refrigeration devices via four liquid ammonia recirculation pumps. Inside the Cold

nia vessels prevent equipment rupture in the event of overpressurization.  Regular inspections and tests are performed to ensure these controls are in good working order.

Five Year Accident History

A review of the facilitys five year accident history showed that there have been no incidents at the facility that meet the RMP criteria for a reportable accident (onsite deaths, injuries, or significant property damage; or known offsite deaths, injuries, property damage, environmental damage, evacuations, or sheltering in place).  In addition, there have been no incidents at the facility in the last five years that resulted in a release of more than the Federal Reportable Quantity (100 pounds). 

Emergency Response Program

Driscolls, Inc. has developed an Emergency Action Plan (EAP) for the purpose of protecting employees and the surrounding community.  The EAP covers procedures for: 1) evacuating and accounting for visitors and employees, 2) dealing with an ammonia release and other foreseeable emergencies that could occur onsite, 3) notifying external agencies and emergency response personnel, and 4) administering first aid measures for ammonia exposure.  Employees are informed of the elements of the EAP.  In the event of an ammonia release, employees will evacuate or shelter-in-place, depending on the nature of the release, and the facility will contact the refrigeration contractor and the fire department (Aromas Tri-County Fire Department, 831-726-3130) for assistance as necessary.

Planned Changes to Improve Safety

Hazard Reviews, Seismic Assessments, and Compliance Audits have been performed on the ammonia refrigeration system, and these studies have resulted in action items to improve safety at the facility.  The recommendations mainly consist of formalizing procedures, implementing practices consistent with industry standards, and performing inspections and tests to maintain the integrity of the equipment.  Driscolls, Inc. has implemented several of these

action items and is moving forward with completing the remaining outstanding recommendations.   In addition, the facility plans to continue providing employees with a safe work environment through continued training on current policies and procedures, and conducting audits to identify deficiencies and make improvements.
